newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan takes delivery of more Patriot launchers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan takes delivery of more Patriot launchers.

text.p: Taiwan on Wednesday took delivery of two more launchers and parts for U.S.-made Patriot missiles that are being bought to guard against attack from China, a local newspaper reported.
The shipment in three containers arrived in Taiwan's northern port of Keelung, the United Evening News said, adding that more missiles and relevant facilities were expected.

Taiwan ordered at least 200 Patriot missiles from the United States in 1993 at a cost of some US$175 million. The deal irked China, which has warned other countries against forging ties with Taiwan and selling arms to the island.
Taiwan took delivery of at least six launch vehicles and a large number of parts and components earlier this month.
The defence ministry declined to comment on the report.
The ministry has remained tight-lipped over the Gulf War-tested anti-aircraft and anti-missile weapons, despite media reports accompanied by pictures of their arrival.

Beijing, which has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a civil war split them in 1949, asserts a right to use force to prevent moves by Taiwan towards independence and away from its advocacy of eventual reunification with the mainland.
China rattled Taiwan with war games and missile tests between 1995 and 1996, held to try to intimidate the island over what Beijing perceived as a growing independence trend.
